bottleneck: Glia — astrocytes, microglia, oligodendrocytes — outnumber neurons and actively shape signaling, yet neuroscience remains neuron-centric: most models, recordings, and theories ignore glial computation entirely. Astrocytes modulate thousands of synapses through calcium waves, microglia prune circuits during development and disease, and oligodendrocytes tune conduction speed — but how glial networks process information is barely characterized. Recording technology is built for spikes, which glia do not produce, so their signaling is systematically invisible to the field's instruments. A brain theory built on half the cells is incomplete by construction.
current_state: Two-photon imaging reveals rich glial calcium signaling, but integrating glia into computational models of brain function is in its infancy, and no major theory of cognition includes them.

sources.title: Brain Connectome: Mapping Neural Networks in Neuroscience

title: Glial computation excluded from brain models
why_it_blocks: Ignoring the brain's most numerous cells guarantees blind spots in every theory of cognition and disease. Glia may hold mechanisms — in sleep, pain, and neurodegeneration — that neurons alone cannot explain.
